title: Companies Act, 2013 — Sections 39 and 42 (Allotment and private placement)

content.overview: No allotment of securities offered to the public shall be made unless the minimum subscription is received. A private placement is an offer to a selected group, by a private placement offer letter, and the money is received only through the banking channel the section requires.
content.glance: No allotment of securities offered to the public shall be made unless the minimum subscription is received. A private placement is an offer to a selected group, by a private placement offer letter, and the money is received only through the banking channel the section requires.
content.study: Companies Act, 2013 — Sections 39 and 42 (Allotment and private placement). No allotment of securities offered to the public shall be made unless the minimum subscription is received. A private placement is an offer to a selected group, by a private placement offer letter, and the money is received only through the banking channel the section requires. The section applies only to the persons, companies, and transactions it names. A filing, approval, or penalty arises only where the section or a rule under it says so. It does not create a power that is reserved to another section or to the Tribunal. Not a verified closure.

sections.heading: Explanation
sections.body: Section 39 is the public-offer allotment condition, with a return of allotment under section 39(4). Section 42 limits the number of persons and requires a separate bank account. A private placement that is a public offer is treated as a public offer and attracts the consequence in section 42.
